source.publication: Rhode Island Retirement Income Tax Guide, Publication 2026-01 (tax year 2025)
source.section: Instructions PDF p.10, Schedule M line 1v; Guide PDF p.15; Guide PDF p.15, Section 2 Example #1; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 55,000.00 + military pension (person 0) 30,000.00 = 85,000.00. Federal taxable income = 85,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 69,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 85,000.00. Line 1v military service pension 30,000.00 (in full, no age or income test). Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 30,000.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 30,000.00 = -30,000.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -30,000.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 85,000.00 + (-30,000.00) = 55,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 55,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 55,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 44,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 44,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 39,000.00. Line 8 tax on 39,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 39,000.00 x 0.0375 = 1462.500000 = 1,462.50. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 1,462.50. Note: Guide Example #1 (Joshua, 62, federal AGI 85,000): no age or income test.
